node.title: (SHARE3-m): the Luroth pullback template and the constant-norm mechanism
node.closure: template plus an existence mechanism; the m = 4 gap is one coincidence
node.statement: Order-3 tuple sharing in the (BIV-CURVE) lane is a Luroth pullback and is a member of the banked Luroth lattice (f_weight2_inverse's global pullback theorem plus payment_completeness's lattice unification). Its x-degree arithmetic is deg_x = k*deg_w, so maximal sharing k = m-1 forces deg_w = 3 exactly and is FREE in the 3(m-1) budget, with waste 3(m-1) mod k reproducing the even-m lost unit at k = 2. Demand: the round-35 quadratic row 3m(m-1)-(rho-1) = 8,22,42 at m = 3,4,5 is superseded by the ceiling row 8,25,47 (printed derivation only at m = 4: 25 = 36+4-15), with calibrations D(2,2) = 8 at m = 3 and D(3,3) = 11 at m = 4 and D_max(m) = (8m-9)-(4m-1) = 4m-8 linear for m >= 7; best-achieved supply 8,12,9 meets demand only at m = 3. Existence mechanism: a 3-sharing pattern is a line through at least 8 of the C(64,3) = 41664 mu_64-split cubics, and since any line joining two cubics of equal root-product preserves that product, the mu_N group structure supplies the sharing at cost 1/N rather than 1/q, refuting the registered q^-12 moment by 3400x. Exhaustively at q = 193 the split cubics fall into 64 equidistributed norm classes of 651, the maximum number of collinear split cubics is 31, and 9152 lines carry at least 8; the lines are structurally forced (fix one root r and vary the other two at fixed product). At m = 4, |W| = 27 = 7m-1 lands exactly, the selection layer is free and k = 8 of 8 is reached, but the slope count is 14 or 15 against the 13 required: m = 4 remains OPEN, one coincidence short, with six classes searched-negative.
